title: Investigate cross-tenant quota bleed during API key exchange and subaccount merges
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Summary: Several customers reported spikes in their quota consumption and unexpected rate-limit rejections immediately following scheduled API key rotations and during a recent subaccount merge. Symptoms look like attribution bleed: usage from one tenant or subaccount being attributed to another, and rate-limiter bucket counts not decrementing as expected after key swaps. This ticket drives the investigation, root cause analysis, and short-term mitigation and long-term fix rollout.

Background: Our attribution pipeline uses a combination of stateless token decoding and an in-memory key->tenant mapping cache to resolve owner, org, and workspace for incoming requests. During a key rotation we write the new key entry and mark the old key as rotated; a background reconciler migrates long-lived claims to the new mapping. Recent deploys introduced an optimization that keeps the in-memory mapping sticky for 10m to reduce DB lookups. Early repros suggest that when a token is rotated and the same raw request hits different frontends, the old in-memory mapping can persist and be used to attribute incoming requests to the wrong owner for a window, which combined with rate-limiter sharding causes quota counters to live under the wrong tenant ID.

Reproduction steps observed: 
1) Customer creates subaccount A and B under the same org, issues API keys KA and KB.
2) Subaccount A rotates key KA -> KA_v2. Rotation writes new mapping but some frontends retain cached mapping for KA that still resolves to A_old_id for ~5-12 minutes.
3) Requests signed with KA_v2 (or expiring old tokens) are routed to frontends with stale cache due to sticky session; those frontends map calls to A_old_id or even to B if some reconciliation race occurred during merge operations.
4) Rate limiter and billing pipeline use the resolved owner ID; quota tokens are consumed from the wrong tenant bucket and usage records are written with incorrect attribution.

Observed evidence and artifacts: 
- Grafana spikes in per-tenant token count aligned to rotation windows: https://grafana.redwood-infra/billing/d/ABC123/tenant-attribution
- Correlated logs showing same request IDs with different resolved_owner values across frontends: log snippets in Confluence doc https://confluence.redwood-infra/space/BILLING/pages/KeyRotationAttributionBug
- Temporary investigation PR adding debug traces: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4872

Impact: 
- Customers seeing unexpected quota exhaustion and denied API calls immediately after rotations/merges. 
- Potential bill disputes if usage permanently misattributed. 
- Risk to SLA and customer trust for Dedicated/Private customers with strict accounting requirements.

Short-term mitigations (prod-safe): 
- Immediately reduce in-memory mapping TTL from 10m to 30s for all frontends to limit exposure window. This can be toggled via feature flag and rolled out incrementally.
- Add strict validation on rotation events: when key rotation is invoked, push an invalidation event to the mapping cache (pub/sub) to sweep all frontends.
- Add a temporary reconciliation job to scan last 48 hours for sudden attribution deltas and create a draft backfill report for impacted customers.

Long-term fixes and deliverables: 
- Fix 1: Change attribution lookup to prefer authoritative DB mapping for rotation events for the first N minutes after rotation; only cache stable keys after a confirmation TTL.
- Fix 2: Make rate limiter owner-key sharding use immutable key IDs (internal key GUID) rather than user-visible owner strings that can move during merges.
- Fix 3: Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate rotation and subaccount merge interleavings; these should run in CI with a synthetic multi-frontend setup.
- Fix 4: Implement a reconciler that can atomically remap in-flight usage buckets when a merge occurs and generate a deterministic migration plan for billing.

Next steps: 
- (Today) Run the TTL rollback and enable cache invalidation events behind a kill-switch. Owner: Aisha. Target: canary 03/14, global 03/15.
- (48h) Launch reconciliation scan and contact affected customers with a preliminary incident summary. Owner: Diego.
- (1 sprint) Implement authoritative-lookup + integration tests. Owner: backend core team.

Notes: Be careful with performance trade-offs: decreasing cache TTL increases DB read load; consider a short-lived edge cache combined with explicit invalidation on rotation. Any migration that changes owner IDs in rate-limiter buckets must be idempotent and replay-safe.
